title: Transductive autoencoder bottleneck features
spec: Build the matrix of Morgan radius-2 bits plus MACCS keys for both training and test molecules together (unsupervised, so test features are allowed). Train a sklearn MLPRegressor with a single hidden layer of 256 ReLU units and a 32-unit bottleneck, which is an autoencoder over this matrix (use two MLPRegressor stages or a manual numpy autoencoder), fit with max_iter=200 and random_state=seed. Take the 32-unit bottleneck activations as dense features and concatenate them with the curated descriptors. Train one XGBoost model on this feature set and rank-average it with the existing members. Labels are never used in the autoencoder.

title: Parameter-free CNS MPO desirability as a rank member
spec: Compute a CNS multiparameter-optimisation style score with no fitted parameters. For each molecule, take RDKit values for ClogP, MW, TPSA, HBD, most basic pKa proxy (count of BASIC_AMINE matches as a 0/1 proxy), and acid count. Map each to a desirability in [0,1] with fixed piecewise-linear ramps (e.g. TPSA full score below 60 and zero above 120, HBD full score at 0 to 1 and zero above 3, MW full score below 360 and zero above 500, ClogP full score in 1 to 3). Sum the six desirabilities into a score in [0,6]. Rank-transform this score on test molecules and add it to the existing rank-sum in fit_predict with weight 0.5 relative to each XGBoost member. No extra learning, and the seed is unused for this member.

title: Multi-scale Morgan counts at radius 1 and 3
spec: Add a fourth feature set built from hashed Morgan count fingerprints at radius 1 with 1024 bits and at radius 3 with 4096 bits, both with includeChirality=False. Train one XGBoost member per set using the existing hyperparameters, and rank-average all members as now. This tests whether the radius-2 Morgan choice is limiting, without changing the other members. Keep the code path identical to the current Morgan generator, just parameterised by radius and size.

title: Input bit-dropout augmentation
spec: Before fitting each XGBoost member, make 3 augmented copies of the training matrix. In each copy, randomly set 10% of the nonzero fingerprint entries to zero (not the curated descriptor columns), with the random generator seeded from seed and the copy index. Stack the original and the 3 copies and fit one XGBoost model on all 4x rows, with the same hyperparameters but 300 rounds. Predict on the unaltered test matrix. Keep the feature sets, rank averaging and everything else unchanged.

title: BCUT eigenvalue descriptors as a fourth XGBoost member
spec: Inside featurize-style code, build a Burden-type matrix per molecule: diagonal entries are atomic properties (Gasteiger charge, Crippen logP contribution, atomic mass scaled, polarizability proxy), off-diagonal entries are 1 for bonded atoms and 0 otherwise. Take the largest 8 and smallest 8 eigenvalues of that matrix as 16 features, with 0 for empty molecules. Train one XGBoost (same settings as the incumbent members) on these BCUT features concatenated with the 10 curated descriptors, and rank-average its test probabilities with the existing three members. Use the seed for XGBoost random_state.

title: Spline-basis additive logistic model on curated descriptors
spec: Build a generalized additive logistic model. For each of the 10 curated descriptors, expand the value into a cubic B-spline basis with 6 knots placed at training-set quantiles, giving about 60 columns. Fit an L2-penalized logistic regression (C around 0.5, lbfgs, max_iter 2000) on the standardized spline columns from the training set only. Add this as a fourth rank-averaged member next to the incumbent XGBoost ensemble. Use scipy.interpolate.BSpline or sklearn SplineTransformer for the basis, and the seed only if a tie-breaking shuffle is needed.

title: Linear SVM with Platt scaling on concatenated Morgan and MACCS bits
spec: Concatenate the 2048 Morgan presence bits and the 167 MACCS bits for each molecule, then fit sklearn LinearSVC (C=0.05, loss='squared_hinge', max_iter 5000, class_weight='balanced', random_state=seed). Convert decision values to probabilities with a Platt sigmoid fitted on the training decision values using a 5-fold inner cross-validation (CalibratedClassifierCV with method='sigmoid'). Add this as a fourth rank-averaged member. A linear max-margin model is a different inductive bias from the tree members and is cheap to fit.

title: Rotation-forest style oblique trees on descriptors plus fingerprints
spec: Replace the XGBoost members with a rotation forest of 200 trees. For each tree, randomly partition the standardised feature space (curated descriptors plus 2048-bit Morgan bits selected to the 300 most frequent in training) into subsets of 10 features. For each subset fit PCA on a seeded 75% bootstrap of the training rows, and stack the rotated components to form the tree's input. Fit a sklearn DecisionTreeClassifier with max_depth=None and min_samples_leaf=2 on the rotated data. Average predicted probabilities across trees. Use the seed for all partitions and bootstraps. This gives oblique splits that tree ensembles on raw bits cannot form.

title: Seed-averaged bagging of the full ensemble with feature-column shuffle
spec: Run the entire three-feature-set XGBoost ensemble across 3 inner seeds derived from the seed argument (seed, seed+1000, seed+2000). In each inner run, apply a random permutation of columns in the 2048-bit Morgan matrix only for the training and test matrices together, which changes which bits share tree splits without changing information. Average the rank-normalised outputs over the 3 inner runs before returning. Keep n_estimators at 500 and reduce n_jobs contention by fitting the inner runs sequentially. Target runtime is under 3 minutes per job, well inside the 10-minute limit.

title: Ionization-corrected logD estimate as a feature
spec: Extend featurize with an estimated distribution-coefficient feature. Count carboxylic acids (existing ACID pattern), basic aliphatic amines (existing BASIC_AMINE pattern), and quaternary or permanently charged nitrogens. Estimate an approximate pKa per group (acid about 4.5, aliphatic amine about 9.5) and compute logD7.4 ~= MolLogP - log10(1 + 10**(7.4 - pKa_acid)*n_acid) - log10(1 + 10**(pKa_base - 7.4)*n_base), clipped to [-5, 8]. Append this logD value and the count of ionised groups to the curated descriptor matrix that feeds the existing ensemble member. Everything else stays the same.

title: RBF-kernel SVM on quantile-scaled curated descriptors
spec: Add a fourth member: an SVC with an RBF kernel (probability=False) on the 10 curated descriptors after quantile transformation to a normal distribution, with statistics fitted on the training molecules only. Set C=1.0 and gamma='scale', and class_weight='balanced'. Use decision_function on the test molecules as the score, rank-normalise it, and add it to the rank-average ensemble with weight 1. The SVM is deterministic, so seed is unused here. This tests a kernel model on descriptors that is different from the earlier Tanimoto SVM and the tree models.

title: Dirichlet bootstrap sample weights per ensemble member
spec: Instead of the usual row subsampling, give each of the three existing XGBoost members a Bayesian bootstrap: draw non-negative weights from a Dirichlet(1,...,1) distribution over the training molecules (scaled so the weights average 1), with a separate draw per member, using a RandomState seeded from the seed argument. Pass them as sample_weight to fit. Set the model's subsample parameter to 1.0 so the weights are the only source of randomness. Keep all hyperparameters otherwise unchanged and rank-average the three members as before.

title: Transductive kNN smoothing of test scores
spec: After computing the ensemble's normalised score for every test molecule, smooth it over the test set itself. Compute Tanimoto similarity between the Morgan bit vectors of all test molecules. For each test molecule, take its k=5 most similar other test molecules (similarity above 0.3, otherwise ignore) and replace its score with a 0.7/0.3 blend of its own score and the similarity-weighted mean of its neighbours' scores. Use only the test-set scores and fingerprints, so no labels are involved and the procedure is consistent across folds. Return the smoothed scores rank-normalised to [0, 1].

title: Polyak-averaged minibatch logistic regression on Morgan counts
spec: Add a fourth member: a logistic regression trained with AdaGrad-style minibatch SGD on 2048-bit hashed Morgan count features, log1p-transformed and standardised using training statistics. Use L2 penalty 1e-4, batch size 64, 30 epochs, and a learning rate of 0.1 decayed as 0.1/sqrt(epoch+1). Shuffle each epoch with a RandomState seeded by the seed argument. Return the average of the weight vectors over the last 10 epochs (Polyak averaging) and use that averaged model for predictions. Rank-normalise its test probabilities and add them to the ensemble sum with weight 1.

title: Functional-group SMARTS count library as a fourth member
spec: Define a fixed list of about 60 SMARTS patterns for groups relevant to BBB penetration: amides, sulfonamides, sulfonyl groups, phenols, anilines, nitro groups, aryl halides, esters, ethers, ureas, carbamates, nitriles, hydroxyl groups, quaternary ammonium, tertiary amines, pyridines, imidazoles, and so on. For each molecule, count matches of each pattern with GetSubstructMatches and build a 60-column integer matrix. Train one XGBoost model (same hyperparameters as the existing members) on this matrix, and add its rank to the ensemble sum. Keep the other three members unchanged.

title: Greedy rule-set learner on curated descriptor thresholds
spec: Replace one fingerprint member with a sequential-covering rule learner. Build candidate single-feature threshold conditions from quantile cut points (10 per descriptor) on the 10 curated descriptors. Greedily grow up to 15 conjunctive rules of length at most 3: each rule is chosen to maximise the Laplace-smoothed precision of positives on the still-uncovered training molecules, then removes the molecules it covers. The score for a molecule is the Laplace-smoothed positive rate of the first rule it matches, or the base rate if none match. Return the normalised score. Use seed only for tie-breaking shuffles. Add it as one rank-averaged member.

title: Pairwise interaction features on the curated descriptors
spec: Extend featurize() so that, in addition to the 10 curated columns, it appends all pairwise products of the continuous columns (TPSA, MolWt, MolLogP, HBD, HBA, rotatable bonds, Fsp3) and the ratio TPSA/MolWt, giving roughly 30 columns. Standardise nothing, since trees are invariant to scale. Use this matrix as the descriptor feature set in the existing XGBoost ensemble (replace the current descriptor-only member, leave the Morgan and atom-pair members unchanged). Seeded XGBoost settings stay as they are.

title: DART booster with dropout over trees
spec: Swap each XGBoost member's booster for DART by passing booster='dart' with rate_drop=0.1, skip_drop=0.5, and one_drop=True. Keep n_estimators near 300 and learning_rate near 0.1, because DART is slower per tree. Predict with the default ntree_limit behaviour. Use only the fingerprint/curated feature sets already in the ensemble. This is a regularization change, as tree dropout is a different regularizer from subsampling and depth limits.

title: Butina-cluster hold-out bagging
spec: Before fitting, cluster the training molecules with Butina clustering on Morgan Tanimoto distances at a 0.6 threshold. Build 12 bags: each bag drops a random 25% of clusters (drawn with the seed) and trains one XGBoost per feature set on the remaining molecules. Average the rank-normalized test predictions over all bags and feature sets. The point is to make each member see a different chemotype mix, which should help generalization to unseen scaffolds. Keep the per-bag XGBoost size small (300 rounds) so the job stays under the 10-minute limit.

title: Donor-acceptor topological-distance histogram
spec: Build a fixed-length feature vector that counts pairs of hydrogen-bond donor atoms and acceptor atoms (use Lipinski-style SMARTS for donors and acceptors) binned by topological shortest-path distance, with bins 1 to 10 and a final overflow bin. Use Chem.GetDistanceMatrix. Treat it as a new feature set and fit one XGBoost member on it inside the existing ensemble loop. Keep the rest of the pipeline unchanged.

title: Greedy forward selection over a pool of precomputed members
spec: Precompute a pool of 6 to 8 cheap members (the existing three XGBoost feature sets plus ExtraTrees on Morgan bits and a logistic regression on descriptors). Score each member's predictions with a stratified 3-fold inner CV on the training data, and run greedy forward selection with replacement (up to 8 steps) on rank-averaged AUROC. Average only the selected members' ranks for the test predictions. Keep the outer fit_predict signature unchanged.

title: L1-logistic gate for feature selection before boosting
spec: Before the XGBoost members are fit, fit an L1-penalised LogisticRegression (solver liblinear) on the concatenated Morgan, atom-pair and MACCS bits, scaled to unit variance. Choose C by a stratified 3-fold inner CV on AUROC over a small grid (0.01, 0.03, 0.1). Keep only the columns with nonzero coefficients (cap at the 400 largest by absolute coefficient) and feed that reduced matrix to each XGBoost member. Use the seed for any shuffling.

title: Element-composition and aromaticity count features
spec: Append a small block of composition features to the curated descriptor matrix in featurize(): counts of N, O, S, F, Cl, Br, I and P atoms, fraction of aromatic heavy atoms, and count of halogens. Compute them from the RDKit mol with simple atom loops. Keep the descriptor block as a separate feature set so it becomes one more XGBoost member in the existing rank-averaged ensemble, with the same XGBoost settings. Do not change the fingerprints or the existing members.

title: Out-of-fold substructure target encoding
spec: Inside fit_predict, build a binary matrix of Morgan radius-2 presence bits for the training molecules. For each bit, compute the smoothed positive rate across training molecules that carry it, with smoothing toward the global prior using m=10 pseudo-counts. Compute these rates out-of-fold with a 5-fold split of the training set (stratified, seeded) so that a training molecule never encodes itself. For each molecule, average the encoded rates over its set bits, and also take min and max, giving a 3-feature summary. Feed these 3 features plus the 10 curated descriptors into a single XGBoost model. Test molecules use rates fitted on the full training set.

title: Out-of-bag early stopping per boosting member
spec: For each of the three existing XGBoost members, draw a bootstrap sample of the training molecules with the seed. Train with a large budget of 1500 rounds using learning rate 0.05 and record the log-loss on the out-of-bag molecules at every round via evals_result. Choose the round count that minimises out-of-bag log-loss, clipped to [150, 800]. Refit a model on the full training set with that round count (not on the bootstrap sample) and use it for prediction. This replaces the fixed 500-round setting for these members and keeps the rest of the ensemble unchanged.

title: Soft distillation from an inner teacher ensemble
spec: Two-stage distillation inside fit_predict. First, train the existing three-member XGBoost ensemble on the training fold and get out-of-fold probabilities for the training molecules with a 4-fold split of the training set. Second, train a student XGBoost regressor (reg:squarederror, 400 rounds, depth 4, learning rate 0.05) on the same fingerprint and descriptor features, with the OOF teacher probabilities as continuous targets. Predict test molecules with the student and average its rank with the teacher's rank 50/50. Use the seed argument in all splits and models.

title: Hashed Morgan count features with adaptive bit-budget by frequency
spec: Instead of the fixed 2048-bit Morgan fingerprint, build the Morgan count fingerprint with unfolded identifiers (GetSparseCountFingerprint, radius 2). Keep only substructure identifiers that occur in at least 5 training molecules and at most 80% of them, then rank these by document frequency and keep the top 1024 as columns. Map test molecules onto the same column list (unseen identifiers are dropped). Train the existing XGBoost member on these columns and rank-average it with the other members. This is a data-driven vocabulary, so it adapts to the training set rather than relying on hash collisions.

title: Pairwise-margin AUROC optimisation of a linear scorer
spec: Add a linear member trained to maximise pairwise ordering directly, which is what AUROC measures. Standardise the curated descriptors and the 2048-bit Morgan presence bits. Sample 200000 random (positive, negative) training pairs per fit (seeded). Minimise the mean logistic loss log(1+exp(-(s_pos - s_neg))) plus an L2 term 1e-3*||w||^2 with a linear score s = X w, using scipy.optimize.minimize (L-BFGS-B) on the pair-difference matrix in mini-batches of 20000 pairs, or with a single full-batch pass if memory permits. Convert the resulting scores to ranks and average them with the XGBoost members. The objective matches the metric, so it may reorder the decision boundary in ways a classification loss does not.

title: Scaffold-grouped chemical complexity and stereochemistry features
spec: Add to featurize: BertzCT (Descriptors.BertzCT), the number of stereocentres found with Chem.FindMolChiralCenters(m, includeUnassigned=True), the number of fused ring systems (count of ring-system components from the RingInfo atom-ring sharing), the number of aromatic rings, and the fraction of heavy atoms that are sp2 carbons. Replace NaN or inf with 0. Append these five to the curated descriptor matrix. Complexity and stereocentre count track natural-product-like and peptidic compounds, which tend to penetrate the BBB less, and they are not captured by the existing ring-skeleton fingerprints.

title: Hashed-size diversity ensemble
spec: Keep the current three-feature-set XGBoost ensemble structure, but build each feature set at three hashing widths: Morgan and atom-pair at 512, 1024 and 4096 bits, and MACCS unchanged. Train one XGBoost model per (feature set, width) pair, so 6 members in total, each with the existing hyperparameters and seed. Rank-average all members with equal weight. The aim is to diversify collision patterns across members rather than to add a new chemical view. Keep the total runtime in budget by reducing n_estimators to 350 for the 4096-bit members.

title: Character n-gram TF-IDF logistic model on SMILES strings
spec: Add a new member that works directly on the raw SMILES text. Use sklearn TfidfVectorizer with analyzer='char', ngram_range=(2,6), min_df=2, sublinear_tf=True, and fit it on train_smiles only. Train LogisticRegression(C=2.0, max_iter=3000, class_weight=None, random_state=seed) on the sparse matrix, predict test probabilities, and rank-average them with the existing XGBoost members (equal weight, then normalise to [0,1]). The text model is trained on a different representation from the fingerprints, so its errors should be partly uncorrelated with theirs.

title: Platt-calibrated gradient boosting with subsampling
spec: Train LightGBM with bagging_fraction=0.7, bagging_freq=1, feature_fraction=0.2, num_leaves=31, min_child_samples=20, 300 trees, and learning_rate 0.05 on Morgan bits. Then wrap it with sklearn CalibratedClassifierCV(method='sigmoid', cv=3) using the training fold. Calibration makes the scores comparable across the ensemble members and can help when they are combined later.

title: Similarity-gated member blending
spec: Replace the fixed equal-weight rank average with a per-test-molecule weight. For each test molecule, compute its maximum Tanimoto similarity to the training set on Morgan bit vectors (radius 2, 2048 bits). Define the gate g = clip((sim_max - 0.3)/0.4, 0, 1). Final score = g * (average of XGBoost member ranks) + (1 - g) * (rank of the curated-descriptor random forest), so that molecules unlike the training set rely on the descriptor model, which generalises better across scaffolds. Rank-normalise the final scores to [0,1]. This only changes how the existing members are combined, so no new models need to be trained.

title: Lossguide growth with a leaf budget
spec: Change the XGBoost members to grow_policy='lossguide' with max_leaves=31 and max_depth=0, keeping learning_rate 0.05, subsample 0.8, colsample_bytree 0.3, min_child_weight 2 and 500 rounds. Lossguide expands the leaf with the largest loss reduction first, so the tree budget is spent where the signal is instead of on uniform depth. Apply this to all three feature sets and rank-average as before. Pass random_state=seed.

title: Drug-likeness rule-violation counts and property ratios
spec: Extend featurize with a few integer and ratio features: the number of Lipinski violations (MW>500, cLogP>5, HBD>5, HBA>10), the number of Veber violations (rotatable bonds>10, TPSA>140), the number of Ghose violations (MW outside 160-480, cLogP outside -0.4 to 5.6, heavy atoms outside 20-70, molar refractivity outside 40-130), and the ratios TPSA/MW, HBD/HBA and cLogP/TPSA (use 0 when the denominator is 0). Keep the existing XGBoost model and feature sets; only the curated descriptor matrix changes.

title: Parzen density-ratio classifier on curated descriptors
spec: Inside fit_predict, quantile-scale the 10 curated descriptors using training-set quantiles (fit on train only, then apply to test). For each test molecule, compute a Gaussian-kernel Parzen estimate of the positive-class density and of the negative-class density over the training molecules, with bandwidth set by Scott's rule on the scaled features. Score = log(p_pos) - log(p_neg) with a small additive epsilon, and return the rank-normalised score in [0, 1]. Use it as one rank-averaged member next to the existing XGBoost ensemble, with weight 1. No randomness is involved, so seed is unused.

title: Spectral embedding of the transductive Tanimoto graph as extra features
spec: Inside fit_predict, stack the training and test Morgan bit vectors. Build a kNN similarity graph over all molecules (k=10 nearest by Tanimoto, symmetrized, edge weights equal to the similarity). Compute the 16 smallest nontrivial eigenvectors of the normalized graph Laplacian with scipy.sparse.linalg.eigsh (or dense numpy.linalg.eigh if the graph is small), using the seed for the initialization where applicable. Append these 16 embedding coordinates to the feature matrix of the Morgan member only, and fit the existing XGBoost model. Training labels are used only in the fit, not in the embedding, so the embedding is unsupervised and transductive; it encodes cluster structure that tree models cannot derive from raw bits.

title: RDKit structural-alert counts as extra curated descriptors
spec: Extend featurize() with counts of structural alerts from rdkit.Chem.FilterCatalog. Build one FilterCatalog for each of PAINS, Brenk and NIH catalogs (FilterCatalogParams with the matching FilterCatalogs enum values). For each molecule, record the number of matching entries per catalog (3 numbers) and the number of distinct alert descriptions (3 numbers). Append these 6 columns to the existing 10 curated descriptors, so the descriptor matrix becomes 16 columns. Leave the fingerprint members and the XGBoost ensemble structure unchanged, and feed the descriptor matrix as an additional XGBoost member, replacing nothing else.

title: Molecular Quantum Numbers replace the MACCS member
spec: Swap the MACCS feature set in fingerprints() for the 42 molecular quantum numbers from rdkit.Chem.rdMolDescriptors.MQNs_(m), which are integer counts of atom types, bond types, polarity and topology. Concatenate them with the 10 curated descriptors to form a 52-column dense matrix. Keep the same three-member XGBoost loop, so the Morgan and atom-pair members are untouched and the MACCS member becomes the MQN-plus-curated member. Keep max_features and the other hyperparameters the same, and use float32 arrays. Compare against the incumbent three-member average on the same 15 folds.

title: Snapshot averaging across boosting rounds
spec: Keep the three-feature-set XGBoost ensemble, but for each model average predictions taken at several boosting stages instead of only the final one. Train once with n_estimators=500, then compute predict_proba with iteration_range=(0, k) for k in {100, 200, 300, 400, 500} and average the resulting probabilities (or ranks) across those stages before the cross-feature-set rank averaging. This adds a cheap schedule-style ensemble over the training trajectory and needs no extra fits.

title: Tanimoto-neighbour residual correction
spec: Inside fit_predict, get out-of-fold predicted probabilities for the training molecules from the existing XGBoost ensemble using a 5-fold split of the training set. Compute residuals r = y - p_oof. For each test molecule, find its k=10 nearest training molecules by Tanimoto similarity on Morgan radius-2 bits and compute a similarity-weighted mean residual (weights = similarity to the power 3). Add this correction, scaled by 0.5, to the ensemble's probability on the test molecule before the final rank step. Clip to [0,1] before ranking. Training molecules' own residuals must never be used for their own correction, which the out-of-fold step guarantees.

title: Covariate-shift importance weighting from a domain classifier
spec: Inside fit_predict, train a small logistic-regression or shallow XGBoost domain classifier to separate the training fingerprints (label 0) from the test fingerprints (label 1), using the Morgan bits. Convert its predicted probabilities p into importance weights p/(1-p), clipped to [0.1, 10] and normalized to mean 1. Use these weights as sample_weight when fitting each existing XGBoost member. The model is then tuned toward the test-set chemistry without using test labels. Keep the code to one helper function.

title: Learning-rate halving on an inner scaffold plateau
spec: For each XGBoost member, split the training molecules into an inner scaffold-grouped 80/20 holdout using seed-derived group assignments. Train with learning rate 0.1 for up to 600 rounds, evaluating inner logloss every 25 rounds. Whenever the inner logloss has not improved for 75 rounds, halve the learning rate and continue from the current booster via xgb_model. Stop when the learning rate falls below 0.00625. Refit the member on the full training set using the same schedule of rounds and learning rates. This adapts the step size to the data without fixing a round count in advance.

title: Pure-numpy message-passing graph neural network
spec: Replace the fingerprint members with a small graph network written in numpy only. Atoms get a one-hot vector (element, degree, aromaticity, formal charge, H count) and bonds get a type vector. Run 3 rounds of message passing: each atom sums transformed neighbour states weighted by a learned bond-type matrix, then applies a ReLU update with hidden size 64. Pool by sum and mean over atoms, then a logistic output. Train with full-batch Adam (lr 0.01, weight decay 1e-4, 300 epochs) on the training molecules, using the seed for weight init. Hand-write the backward pass or use a finite-difference-free manual gradient; keep the total fit time under 60 seconds per fold. Rank-average its test probabilities with the incumbent ensemble.

title: MinMax-kernel ridge classifier on atom-pair counts
spec: Replace the tree members with kernel ridge regression on the 2048-bit atom-pair count vectors, using the MinMax (generalised Jaccard) kernel K(a,b)=sum_i min(a_i,b_i)/sum_i max(a_i,b_i), computed as a dense train-by-train matrix. Solve (K + lambda I) alpha = y_pm with lambda=1.0 via a Cholesky solve, where y_pm is the labels mapped to plus or minus one. Score test molecules by K_test @ alpha and return rank-normalised scores. The kernel is count-aware, unlike the binary Tanimoto SVC already tried, and needs no hyperparameter search beyond lambda.

title: Atom-level multiple-instance model with max pooling
spec: Replace one ensemble member with a multiple-instance learner. For each molecule, every heavy atom is an instance described by a vector of its element, degree, formal charge, aromaticity, H count, ring membership and a Morgan radius-1 environment hashed to 256 bits. Train a logistic regression on instances, where each instance inherits its molecule's label. The molecule score is the max over its atoms of the instance logit, aggregated with a log-sum-exp (temperature 1) so that the score is smooth. Fit the instance model by gradient descent with L2 regularisation (lambda=1e-3) for 200 steps of full-batch L-BFGS via scipy.optimize.minimize with the EM-style re-assignment of the label-positive instances described as: keep only instances whose current logit is in the top 50% of each positive molecule. Rank-average the resulting molecule scores with the existing XGBoost members.

title: Curriculum two-stage XGBoost
spec: Inside fit_predict, for each feature set, first fit a cheap XGBoost (150 rounds, depth 4) on the training fold and get out-of-fold predictions from a 4-fold split of the training molecules only. Keep the 75% of training molecules with the smallest OOF log-loss as stage-1 data, and train the depth-5, 500-round model on that subset. Then continue boosting from that model (xgb_model argument of fit) on the full training set for 200 more rounds at learning rate 0.02. Everything is seeded by the seed argument. The rest of the ensemble and rank averaging stay unchanged.

title: Mean-teacher MLP with bit-dropout consistency
spec: Build a two-layer MLP on the 2048-bit Morgan presence bits (hidden 256, ReLU, dropout 0.3). Keep an exponential-moving-average copy of the weights (decay 0.99) as the teacher. Each minibatch, feed the student one view with random 20% bit dropout and the teacher a different view with 10% dropout. Loss is binary cross-entropy on labelled rows plus a consistency term, the mean squared difference between student and teacher sigmoid outputs, weighted by 1.0 after a 10-epoch ramp-up. Train for 60 epochs with Adam at lr 1e-3, batch 64. Return the EMA teacher's sigmoid output on test molecules, and rank-average it into the existing ensemble.

title: Logit-space trimmed mean across ensemble members
spec: Replace the final sum of per-member rankdata values in fit_predict with an aggregation in logit space. For each of the three XGBoost members, convert the predicted probability p to logit(clip(p, 1e-6, 1-1e-6)). Stack the three logit vectors for each test molecule and take the trimmed mean that drops the minimum and maximum values, which with three members means taking the median. Then pass the aggregated score through a sigmoid and apply the same min-max normalization as before. This is an aggregator change only: the three XGBoost fits, their features and hyperparameters stay identical, so the difference isolates the effect of robust combination.

title: Label spreading over a Tanimoto kNN graph (transductive)
spec: Build a graph over training and test molecules together. Use Morgan bit vectors and connect each node to its k=10 nearest neighbours by Tanimoto similarity, with edge weights equal to similarity raised to the power 3. Initialize training nodes with their labels (0 or 1) and test nodes with 0.5. Iterate label spreading, F <- alpha * S F + (1 - alpha) * Y0, with alpha=0.9 for 50 steps, clamping training nodes to their labels at each step. Output the converged test-node scores, rank-averaged with the XGBoost ensemble. This is a graph-based semi-supervised method, distinct from the earlier self-training attempt.

title: Clipped-gradient Adam fit of a shallow neural network on count features
spec: Add a small neural network member: a single hidden layer of 64 ReLU units on Morgan count features (log1p transformed) plus the 10 curated descriptors standardised. Train with Adam (lr 1e-3, batch size 64, 60 epochs), gradient-norm clipping at 1.0, and weight decay 1e-4, using numpy only. Use the seed for initialisation and shuffling. Average the outputs of 3 such networks trained with different seeds derived from the seed argument, and rank-average the result with the existing XGBoost members at equal weight.

title: Locally weighted logistic regression over Tanimoto neighbourhoods
spec: Add a local model member. For each test molecule, take the 150 most similar training molecules by Tanimoto similarity on the 2048-bit Morgan bits, weight them by similarity squared, and fit a weighted L2 logistic regression (C=0.3, max_iter=200) on the 10 curated descriptors, standardised using training statistics. The member's score is the local logistic probability for that test molecule. Average its ranks with the existing XGBoost member ranks at equal weight. Pass the seed as random_state wherever a solver accepts it.

title: Spectral embedding combined with ExtraTrees
spec: Append 16 spectral-embedding coordinates to the curated descriptors. Build a symmetrised k=10 nearest-neighbour graph over all molecules (train plus test together, transductive) using Tanimoto similarity on Morgan bits. Compute the 16 smallest nontrivial eigenvectors of the normalised graph Laplacian, and use them as features. Fit ExtraTreesClassifier(n_estimators=500, max_features=0.3, min_samples_leaf=2, random_state=seed) on these features and rank-average it with the existing XGBoost members at equal weight. This recombines two previously helpful pieces and needs a replicate run to confirm.

title: Laplace-approximate Bayesian logistic regression with predictive variance
spec: Add a Bayesian linear member on the 10 curated descriptors plus the 2048-bit Morgan bits reduced by keeping only bits set in at least 5 training molecules. Fit MAP weights with a Gaussian prior of precision 1.0 using L-BFGS. Compute the Hessian at the MAP, invert it to get the posterior covariance, and form the posterior predictive logit for each test molecule as mean times variance-adjusted scaling: logit divided by sqrt(1 plus pi times predictive variance over 8). Use the adjusted probability as the member's score and rank-average it with the existing XGBoost members at equal weight.

title: Weisfeiler-Lehman subtree kernel SVM
spec: Add a graph-kernel member. For each molecule, start from atom labels (atomic number, degree, formal charge, aromaticity, total H count) and run 3 Weisfeiler-Lehman refinement iterations: at each step relabel every atom by hashing its label together with the sorted labels of its neighbours. Count all labels from all iterations into one sparse count vector per molecule, with hashes folded into 4096 buckets. Build the linear kernel matrix from these count vectors, normalised by the square root of self-similarity. Fit SVC(kernel='precomputed', C=1.0) on the training kernel and take decision_function for test-vs-train rows. Rank-average this member with the existing XGBoost members at equal weight. Leave all other code unchanged.
